knowledge:
- key_parameters: mixture.method=Method for mixture modeling, e.g., "vdp" (variational Dirichlet process) ;; pca.basis=Logical, whether to use PCA basis (e.g., pca.basis = TRUE) ;; plot_mode=Mode for plotting responses, options include "pca", "network", "heatmap", "boxplot_data", "response.barplot" ;; two.sided=Logical for plot_scale indicating if the color scale is two-sided ;; speedup=Option to consider with large datasets to speed up computation
- alternatives: None mentioned, but the package is partially based on agglomerative independent variable group analysis (AIVGA) and variational Dirichlet process Gaussian mixture models
- when_to_use: When analyzing condition-specific network activation patterns across versatile collections of functional measurements (e.g., gene expression data) and interaction networks, or when seeking to identify subnetworks with alternative states
- pitfalls: With large datasets, computation can be slow (suggests using the 'speedup' option); cluster indices may switch due to unidentifiability when comparing known and estimated mixture components

workflows.name: network_functional_response_analysis
workflows.intent: Detect and visualize subnetworks with context-specific activation patterns using functional data and a network.
input: D (matrix of functional measurements, e.g., gene expression data where rows are samples and columns are genes/features)
network (matrix or network format representing interaction network topology)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit NetResponse model using detect.responses ;; 2. Extract subnetworks using get.subnets ;; 3. Visualize responses using plot_responses (PCA, network, heatmap, boxplot) ;; 4. Plot color scale using plot_scale ;; 5. Retrieve soft and hard cluster assignments using sample2response and response2sample ;; 6. Retrieve model parameters using get.model.parameters
workflows.code:
res <- generate.toydata(Dim = 3, Nc = 3, Ns = 200, sd0 = 3, rgam.shape = 1, rgam.scale = 1)
D <- res$data
component.means <- res$means
component.sds   <- res$sds
sample2comp     <- res$sample2comp

# Use fully connected network
network <- matrix(rep(1, 9), nrow = 3)

# Various network formats are supported, see help(detect.responses) for
# details. With large data sets, consider the 'speedup' option.
set.seed(4243)
res <- detect.responses(D, network, mixture.method = "vdp", pca.basis = TRUE)

# List subnets (each is a list of nodes)
subnet.id <- names(get.subnets(res))[[1]]

library(ggplot2)
vis <- plot_responses(res, subnet.id, plot_mode = "pca")

# Modify the resulting ggplot2 object to enhance visualization
p <- vis$p # Pick the ggplot2 object from results
p <- p + geom_point(size = 3) # Modify point size
print(p)

vis <- plot_responses(res, subnet.id, plot_mode = "network")

vis <- plot_responses(res, subnet.id, plot_mode = "heatmap")

vis <- plot_responses(res, subnet.id, plot_mode = "boxplot_data")

plot_scale(vis$breaks, vis$palette, two.sided = TRUE)

subnet.id <- 'Subnet-1'

# Sample - response probabilities (soft cluster assignment)
response.probs <- sample2response(res, subnet.id)
tail(round(response.probs, 6))

# Sample - response hard assignments
hard.clusters <- response2sample(res, subnet.id)
print(hard.clusters)

params <- get.model.parameters(res, subnet.id)
names(params)

workflows.name: nonparametric_gaussian_mixture_modeling
workflows.intent: Fit an infinite Gaussian mixture model with a Variational Dirichlet Process approximation on multi-dimensional data.
input: D (matrix of multi-dimensional data where rows are samples and columns are features)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit VDP mixture model using vdp.mixt ;; 2. Extract estimated centroids ;; 3. Retrieve hard mixture component assignments
workflows.code:
# Generate 2-dimensional simulated data with 3 clusters
res <- generate.toydata(Dim = 2, Nc = 3, Ns = 200, sd0 = 3, rgam.shape = 1, rgam.scale = 1)

D <- res$data
real.means <- res$means
real.sds   <- res$sds
real.sample2comp     <- res$sample2comp

# Infinite Gaussian mixture model with
# Variational Dirichlet Process approximation
mixt <- vdp.mixt( D )

# Centroids of the detected Gaussian components
estimated.means <- mixt$posterior$centroids

# The colors denote the known clusters
# The blue ball denotes the original (known) cluster centroids and
# the triangle denotes the estimated centroids
plot(D, col = real.sample2comp, pch = 1)
points(real.means, col = "blue", pch = 16, cex = 2)
points(estimated.means, col = "blue", pch = 17, cex = 2)

# Hard mixture component assignment for each sample
estimated.sample2comp <- apply(mixt$posterior$qOFz, 1, which.max)

# Compare known and estimated mixture components
# (note that cluster indices may have switched due to unidentifiability)
# nearly all samples have one-to-one match between the real and estimated
# clusters
head(table(estimated.sample2comp, real.sample2comp))
